title: Living stones (1 Peter 2:1–10)
hookLine: you are living stones built into a spiritual house
tomorrow: what do you say when a friend asks why you even believe?

cards: Stones don't breathe. They don't grow, or choose where they go; they sit where someone sets them. So 1 Peter says something that sounds like a mistake: "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house."
Lively stones. Living ones. How can a stone be alive?
The letter has already given the clue, a few words earlier, and it starts with one particular stone: the one the builders threw away.

teach.b: Here's the clue. Jesus is "a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious." Rejected, put to death, and alive again: that's yesterday's living hope, turned into stone.
Then the letter quotes an old song: "the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner." The reject ends up holding the walls together. So here's the puzzle solved.
The stones are alive because the stone they're built on is alive. People come to him, and they're fitted in around him, and the house grows.
And look at the shape of it: not bricks pressed from one mold, all the same size, but stones, each its own shape, each with a place.

Then the house needs priests, and the letter calls the readers "a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people." Peculiar, in the King James, means belonging to God, not strange.

teach.h: A ROYAL PRIESTHOOD, READ TWO WAYS.
teach.b: Churches read the royal priesthood in their own ways. Protestant teaching speaks of the priesthood of all believers.
Catholic and Orthodox teaching says all the baptized share in Christ's priesthood, alongside ordained priests who serve at the altar.
And then the line that holds it together: "Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God."

how: Christians use 1 Peter 2 when they speak of the church as people rather than a building, and some churches read it when a new church is dedicated.

games.q: your church youth group is planning a service day. one kid says there's no point in him coming: he's not good at anything they need. what fits 1 Peter 2's picture?
o: only the strongest stones get used in a wall.
every stone has its own shape and its own place.
he should wait until he's more like the others.
games.why: lively stones built up a spiritual house: a wall of different stones, fitted around the one the builders rejected.

practice: Pick up something small and solid: a stone if there's one nearby, or a key or a coin. Close your hand around it and feel its weight and its edges, the shape that's only its own.
For the sit, let it stand for one stone set into something bigger than itself.
